title: Med-REFL: Medical Reasoning Enhancement via Self-Corrected Fine-grained Reflection
authors_zh: Hongxian Yang、Jiayu Qian、Segao Peng、Haoyu Zhang、Lu-An Huang、MC Tan、Shi-An Huang
paper_type_zh: 医学推理偏好数据与自我反思方法论文
best_for_zh: 研究医学大模型、推理纠错或偏好优化的读者。
one_line: Med-REFL creates self-corrected fine-grained reflection preference pairs for medical reasoning optimization.
Med-REFL 将细粒度自我反思转化为医学推理的偏好对，用于纠错式偏好优化。
why: It supplies a preference-data object that targets error correction within medical reasoning rather than only final-answer selection.
inclusion_reason: Med-REFL releases reflection-derived medical preference pairs for preference optimization of medical reasoning models.

title: Problem
问题
html: Large reasoning models perform well in mathematics and code but transfer less reliably to medicine, where a correct final option can hide unsafe or unsupported intermediate reasoning. Expert annotation of every reasoning and reflection step is expensive. The paper asks whether medical questions can be decomposed into fine-grained reasoning paths, automatically evaluated, and converted into preference supervision that teaches a model to detect and repair its own reasoning errors.
大型推理模型在数学和代码任务上表现突出，但迁移到医学领域时稳定性较差；即使最终选项正确，中间推理仍可能包含不安全或缺乏依据的步骤，而逐步专家标注成本很高。论文研究能否将医学问题拆解为细粒度推理路径，自动评价每一步及其反思，并转化为偏好监督，使模型学习识别和修正自身推理错误。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html: Med-REFL is a tree-of-thought data-construction and training framework that evaluates fine-grained medical reasoning and reflection, then converts better and worse trajectories into DPO pairs. The authors release Med-REFL-DPO and related reflection data, allowing the supervision object to include not only final answers but also the quality of corrections applied to intermediate steps. The central contribution is an automated preference pipeline for medical self-reflection rather than a new medical base model.
Med-REFL 是一种基于 tree-of-thought 的数据构造与训练框架，它评价细粒度医学推理及反思，并将较优与较差的轨迹转化为 DPO 偏好对。作者开放 Med-REFL-DPO 及相关反思数据，使监督对象不仅包含最终答案，还覆盖中间步骤被如何纠正及纠正质量。其核心贡献是医学自反思偏好数据的自动构造流程，而不是提出新的医学基础模型。

title: Method
方法
html: The pipeline samples medical questions and expands several candidate reasoning branches. It scores intermediate steps, generates reflections on weak steps, and evaluates whether the revised continuation improves correctness and reasoning quality. Better corrected paths become chosen records and inferior or uncorrected paths become rejected records. A medical reasoning model is then optimized with these preference pairs, while answer correctness and reflection scores act as the main acceptance signals. The released repository contains data, checkpoints, and scripts for construction and training.
流程先采样医学问题，并扩展多条候选推理分支；随后对中间步骤评分，为薄弱步骤生成反思，再判断修订后的后续推理是否改善答案正确性与过程质量。较优的纠正路径被设为 chosen，较差或未纠正路径被设为 rejected，形成医学 DPO 数据。模型再利用这些偏好对优化，其中答案正确性和反思评分共同决定样本去留。官方仓库开放数据、checkpoint 及构造和训练脚本。

title: Evidence
证据
html: The paper evaluates Med-REFL on MedQA-USMLE and additional medical QA benchmarks, reporting average gains up to 4.11 percentage points and a further 4.13-point improvement over strong 7B/8B results. Comparisons include models trained without fine-grained reflection and tests on datasets outside the main construction source, providing both mechanism and transfer evidence. The released data and code improve reproducibility. These results support better benchmark reasoning under the tested models, but they do not verify clinical decision quality or patient safety.

论文在 MedQA-USMLE 及其他医学问答 benchmark 上评测 Med-REFL，报告平均最高提升 4.11 个百分点，并在强 7B/8B 模型基础上进一步提升 4.13 个百分点。对照包含未使用细粒度反思的训练方式，同时在主构造来源之外的数据集测试，因而同时提供机制和迁移证据。官方开放数据与代码也提高了可复现性。结果支持所测模型的 benchmark 推理改进，但不能验证临床决策质量或患者安全。

title: Novelty
新意
html: Previous medical reasoning methods commonly use final-answer supervision, whole-trace distillation, retrieval, or undifferentiated self-reflection. Med-REFL changes the supervision granularity by scoring individual reasoning branches and the corrections applied to them, then constructing explicit chosen–rejected records. Its novelty is the coupling of fine-grained reflection evaluation with preference-data generation. Tree-of-thought search, self-reflection, and DPO are individually established techniques; the new element is their medical data contract and automated pairing rule.
以往医学推理方法常使用最终答案监督、整条轨迹蒸馏、检索增强或不区分质量的自反思。Med-REFL 将监督粒度改为评价具体推理分支及其纠正，并据此构造明确的 chosen–rejected 记录。其新意是把细粒度反思评价与偏好数据生成绑定起来。tree-of-thought、自反思和 DPO 单独来看均非新技术，真正变化在于面向医学的反馈契约和自动配对规则。

title: Limitations
局限
html: The preference labels rely on model-based scoring and answer-level medical benchmarks, so the verifier may reward persuasive but clinically incomplete reasoning. Multiple-choice questions provide clearer correctness signals than open-ended diagnosis or treatment planning, limiting transfer. Synthetic reflections can inherit the generator’s medical misconceptions, and the paper does not replace specialist review. Reuse should audit intermediate claims against trusted medical sources, report verifier disagreement, and avoid treating benchmark gains as permission for autonomous clinical use.
偏好标签依赖模型评分和答案级医学 benchmark，因此 verifier 可能奖励表达流畅但临床信息不完整的推理。选择题比开放式诊断或治疗规划更容易获得明确正确性信号，限制了外推范围。合成反思也可能继承生成模型的医学误解，不能替代专科医生审核。复用时应依据可信医学资料抽查中间主张、报告 verifier 分歧，并避免把 benchmark 提升解释为可自主临床使用。

title: Usefulness
用途
html: Researchers can reuse Med-REFL-DPO to study preference optimization for medical reasoning or use the pipeline to construct domain-specific correction pairs from another medical QA set. The reflection records are also useful for training critics or evaluating whether a model can identify the first weak step. Success should be measured with held-out medical tasks and expert review of reasoning, not accuracy alone. The method is unsuitable when questions lack a reliable answer key or when no qualified reviewer can audit generated medical claims.
研究者可直接使用 Med-REFL-DPO 研究医学推理偏好优化，也可将流程迁移到其他医学问答集，构造领域专用纠正偏好对。反思记录还可用于训练 critic，或评估模型能否定位首个薄弱步骤。有效性应通过留出医学任务和专家过程审核共同判断，而不能只看 accuracy。当问题缺少可靠答案键，或没有合格人员审计生成的医学主张时，不适合直接采用该方法。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html: Med-REFL treats reflection quality as a data object rather than an unverified prompt trick. Its key sequence is branch generation, step scoring, reflection, correction evaluation, and DPO pairing. The released artifacts include preference and reflection data plus code. Reported gains reach 4.11 points on average and 4.13 points beyond strong 7B/8B baselines. The main risk is that automatic evaluators can confuse answer agreement with clinically sound reasoning, so expert auditing of intermediate content is the required reuse check.
Med-REFL 将反思质量作为可监督的数据对象，而不是未经验证的提示技巧。关键流程是生成分支、逐步评分、产生反思、评价纠正，再形成 DPO 偏好对。官方开放偏好与反思数据及代码。论文报告平均最高提升 4.11 个百分点，并在强 7B/8B baseline 上进一步提高 4.13 个百分点。最大风险是自动 evaluator 可能把答案一致误认为临床推理可靠，因此复用前必须由专家审计中间内容。
